01

Setting specification

Task

Find an approximate zero of $F+\partial r$. At a solution, a convex subgradient of $r$ at $z$ cancels the vector $F(z)$. Return a point $\widehat z$ whose displacement under the full composite resolvent meets the accuracy guarantee.

$$ 0\in F(z)+\partial r(z). $$

Admissible model

The function $F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ is $\beta$-Lipschitz, and $r$ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. There exists $z^\star$ satisfying $0\in(F+\partial r)(z^\star)$ and $\|z_0-z^\star\|_2\le R$.

For every $(z,v)\in\operatorname{graph}(F+\partial r)$, $\langle v,z-z^\star\rangle\ge-\rho\|v\|_2^2$. The public fixed step size satisfies $0\le\rho<\eta<1/\beta$.

Oracle interface

Public inputs include dimension $d$ and $B$, $R$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, $\eta$, $\rho$, $\sigma$, together with the stated initial point and feasible geometry. Hidden analytic representations are not revealed.

$$ z\longmapsto G_F(z;\xi),\qquad(\gamma,u)\longmapsto\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(u). $$

Fresh responses are conditionally unbiased and satisfy $\mathbb{E}[\|G_F(z;\xi)-F(z)\|_2^2\mid\mathcal{H},z]\le B^2\|z-z_0\|_2^2+\sigma^2$. Samples cannot be reused, and the proximal interface is exact.

The operations $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(u)=\arg\min_v\{r(v)+\|v-u\|_2^2/(2\gamma)\}$ and $\gamma>0$ are available. The resolvent of the entire unknown $F+\partial r$ is not supplied.

Output

Return $\widehat{z}\in\mathbb{R}^d$.

The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

The loss is the Euclidean distance from the returned point to its image under the full composite resolvent at the fixed step size $\eta$. For every admissible instance and legal stochastic feedback mechanism, the expected displacement must be at most $\varepsilon$. The expectation includes the algorithm's private randomness and the fresh oracle responses.

The full composite resolvent defines the error. The available oracle supplies stochastic evaluations of the operator term and the exact proximal map of the convex term.

$$ \|\widehat{z}-J_{\eta(F+\partial r)}(\widehat{z})\|_2. $$

Define $J_{\eta(F+\partial r)}=(\operatorname{Id}+\eta(F+\partial r))^{-1}$; $\eta\beta<1$ ensures the map is single-valued on the whole space. The error is not divided by $\eta$ and is not tangent residual at the original output.

Resource accounting

Fresh-sample operator calls $N_{\rm sample}$ and proximal calls are recorded separately. The primary comparison uses expected $N_{\rm sample}$.

Use expected work on the worst instance. The algorithm stops almost surely, with call count $\tau$ satisfying $\sup_I\mathbb{E}[\tau]\le N$. This does not require every execution path to finish within $N$ calls.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Arbitrary measurable sequential adaptive randomized algorithms are allowed. The private seed is independent of the hidden instance. Queries, stopping, and output may use the full history, without additional span, zero-respecting, communication, or memory restrictions.

Choose one algorithm, then require the guarantee for every admissible instance and stochastic-feedback mechanism.

$$ \mathbb{E}\!\left[\|\widehat{z}-J_{\eta(F+\partial r)}(\widehat{z})\|_2\right]\le\varepsilon. $$

Expectation is outside the complete error expression; internal maxima or suprema are not moved outside it.

Budget convention
expected total fresh stochastic operator calls; randomized multilevel inner work

Solving Stochastic Variational Inequalities without the Bounded Variance Assumption ↗
Conditions
Require $0\le\rho<\eta<1/\beta$. Exact $\operatorname{prox}_r$ is available, but the full resolvent appearing in the performance measure is not an additional oracle.; The adopted range requires the inner strong-monotonicity modulus $1-\eta\beta>0$; the endpoint $\eta=1/\beta$ is excluded.; Without an explicit conversion, resolvent displacement at an output point cannot be interpreted as its tangent residual.
Dimension conditions
The upper bound holds in every admissible finite dimension. The lower bound applies only in its separately stated dimension window.
Algorithm scope
See ALGORITHMS. The upper bound uses the specified algorithm, and the lower bound covers only its explicitly stated algorithm class.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Oracle correspondence
Use only primitive operations recorded under ORACLE. Unknown inner solutions and reduced gradients are not supplied for free.
Guarantee conversion
The error criterion, sources of randomness, and expectation/probability quantifiers match this specification. Any conversion is explained separately below.
Output rule
Outputs belong to the declared space and are evaluated by this profile's METRIC. Different gaps, norms, and squared norms are not interchanged.
Resource conversion
All resource costs come from one algorithm or one hard construction. Initialization and nested calls are included.
Constants
Use the source theorem’s universal constants except where derivative order or structural budgets are explicitly fixed. Unspecified sufficient thresholds remain symbolic.
Logarithmic factors
Accuracy logarithms remain unexpanded. Hidden constants may depend on all declared fixed structural parameters.
Derivation
Use only the strict-interior range $\rho<\eta<1/\beta$. Lipschitz continuity makes $I+\eta F$ strongly monotone with modulus at least $1-\eta\beta>0$, and adding $\eta\partial r$ preserves this property. The full resolvent is therefore single-valued and everywhere defined. Constants in Appendices C.1 and C.5 of the source are finite for each fixed strict-interior parameter choice, giving the upper bound through fresh operator samples and proximal access to $r$. The endpoint $\eta=1/\beta$ is not included automatically.
Scope qualification
The corresponding FBF/KM methods use stochastic samples, randomized output indices, or random MLMC work.
Comparison argument
No matching lower has been independently verified in this native goal/oracle/noise specification.
